tasks.short: Negotiate collective agreements and advise on their interpretation.

steps.what: Find current agreements, amendments and earlier interpretations.
Calculate the cost of bargaining options.
Agree negotiation priorities, limits and escalation points.
Negotiate proposals and concessions with employee or union representatives.
Draft agreed wording and identify unresolved clauses.

loop.input: Current agreement, approved negotiation notes and provisional terms.
loop.output: Agreement redline with source references and unresolved clauses.
loop.check: Validate clause references and numerical terms; specialist checks every substantive change against negotiated terms.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per clause; unresolved wording returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot reliably express changes to varied negotiated language.

steps.what: Approve final terms and complete the required signing or ratification process.
File the signed agreement and update effective dates and review reminders.
Interpret applicable agreement clauses for a specific employee case.

loop.input: Minimised case facts, applicable signed agreement and approved interpretation records.
loop.output: Draft interpretation citing exact clauses, effective dates and missing facts.
loop.check: Check source versions and quotations; HR manager checks applicability and conflicting interpretations.
loop.stop: One answer and one correction pass; missing facts or conflicting clauses produce an escalation note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case wording and clause interactions exceed fixed lookup rules.

steps.what: Explain the interpretation and discuss disputed meaning.

tasks.design: Configure versioned agreements and reminders in the {CLM}, with deterministic cost scenarios built from the {HCM} and {PAYROLL}. Bounded drafting loops prepare redlines and cited interpretations in the {DOCS}; people retain negotiation, final approval and disputed interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement versions, payroll assumptions and negotiation notes sit in separate places. Drafting support needs reliable clause references and access to confidential material.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls and simple calculation code cover much of the preparation. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, while bounded language models can draft from supplied sources.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, bargaining leverage and ambiguous concessions remain difficult. National rules determine representation, consultation and ratification; GDPR governs personal case data.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, judge concessions and preserve a working relationship after a difficult settlement.

ambition.what: Costed concession review between bargaining sessions

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing concessions before meetings. Existing negotiation limits remain; any wider mandate still requires leadership approval.

reach.task: Prepare clause comparisons and bargaining impact assessments.
reach.learn: Agreement versioning, bargaining mandates and the difference between precedent and binding interpretation.

evidence.claim: Versioned records, deterministic costing and source-grounded drafting are feasible building blocks; the digest supplies no bargaining automation case.
A Danish study covering 11 occupations including HR reported 2.8% of hours saved by chatbots; it does not establish savings for bargaining.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its conditions and exceptions.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Signed agreements and approved notes can be accessed with version history and role-based permissions.
Existing configuration supports document filing and reminders; otherwise integration effort increases.
Build ranges cover working effort for one agreement scope. Consultation and bargaining can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Applicable countries, agreements, representative bodies and ratification requirements.
Quality of agreement versions and historical interpretation records.
Available interfaces, access rights and approved model processing arrangements.
Who may approve concessions, interpretations and final commitments.
research_questions: Can cost scenarios reproduce a previously settled agreement using historical payroll inputs?
Can reviewers trace every drafted clause to an agreed source without adding concessions?
Which interpretation categories reliably require legal or representative escalation?
new_work: Maintain effective dates, approved interpretations and calculation assumptions.
Resolve missing sources, disputed wording and access exceptions.
Check integrations and remove obsolete agreement versions from retrieval.

tasks.short: Advise managers on employment policies and recommend policy changes.

steps.what: Receive a manager's query and open a confidential case.
Clarify facts, immediate concerns and the manager's intended action.
Find relevant policies, guidance and earlier approved advice.
Assess the case and prepare advice or a policy change recommendation.

loop.input: Minimised case facts and applicable approved policies and legal guidance.
loop.output: Draft advice separating sourced requirements, options, missing facts and proposed policy changes.
loop.check: Validate citations and versions; HR manager checks reasoning, proportionality and need for legal advice.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported conclusions or conflicting guidance go to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text facts must be related to policies with context-dependent exceptions.

steps.what: Explain advice, challenge assumptions and agree appropriate next steps.
Review proposed policy changes and authorise required consultation or adoption.
Publish approved policy versions and update guidance links.

tasks.design: Configure confidential intake in the {HELPDESK} and versioned policy retrieval from the {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts cited advice for HR review; the {WORKFLOW} publishes policy changes only after the required consultation and approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depends on sensitive facts, local rules and policy versions. Shared inboxes preserve conversations but make precedents and access controls difficult to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Case permissions, versioned search and approval workflows already cover the records work. A bounded model can prepare a sourced first draft from approved material.
tasks.still_hard: Harassment, discrimination and conflicting accounts require careful fact finding and independent judgement. GDPR applies to case data; national rules govern employment procedures and consultation, while the EU AI Act requires assessment if scope expands into employment decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Notice fear, retaliation risk or missing context, and challenge a manager without closing down disclosure.

ambition.what: Monthly review of recurring policy exceptions

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time finding policy text and drafting routine explanations, leaving more time for sensitive conversations and recurring problems. They can propose policy priorities from case patterns; formal policy and employment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review recurring policy exceptions for unequal treatment.
reach.learn: Evidence standards, protected characteristics, confidentiality and the limits of small-group comparisons.

evidence.claim: Confidential case configuration, versioned search and bounded advice drafting are feasible; near-total automation is not established by the supplied evidence.
The AskHR case reports first-year HR NPS of minus 35 when managers lost HR partners and phone access, supporting retention of human advice channels.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its conditions and exceptions.
AI Act Annex III covers specified employment uses; applicability depends on the system's intended purpose.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
A confidential case queue exists or can be configured; automatic intake captures requests without deciding their merits.
Policy amendments are conditional branches; shares represent the average workload across advice cases.
Required consultation is completed before adoption. Consultation response is an input from that separate process.
Build ranges cover working effort for a limited policy set; formal consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Applicable national rules and consultation requirements.
Case access boundaries and arrangements for highly sensitive allegations.
Which guidance is approved, current and authoritative.
Policy approval rights and thresholds for legal escalation.
Whether routine enquiries and formal complaints currently use separate procedures.
research_questions: Can retrieval consistently select the correct policy version and jurisdiction?
Which advice categories are safe to draft, and which should immediately reach a specialist?
Do case patterns reveal policy problems without exposing identifiable employees?
new_work: Review citations, recommendations and missing facts.
Maintain policy ownership, versions and escalation criteria.
Handle unsupported answers and preserve direct access to HR.
Review aggregate case themes before proposing policy changes.

tasks.short: Plan and deliver new employee orientation.

steps.what: Check incoming starters, roles, locations and start dates.
Arrange sessions, speakers and invitations.
Assemble role and location materials from the standard orientation content.
Welcome starters, explain organisational objectives and discuss their questions.
Introduce team priorities and connect starters with colleagues.
Record attendance and send outstanding learning and follow-up reminders.
Review starter feedback and choose changes for the next cohort.

tasks.design: Use starter events from the {HCM} to configure bookings in the {CALENDAR} and enrolments in the {LMS}. A deterministic generator assembles approved modules from the {DOCS}, while attendance confirmations drive completion records and reminders. People deliver the welcome and use a feedback dashboard to improve the next cohort.
tasks.previous_blocker: Starter changes, speaker availability and content variants require coordination across systems. Small cohorts made bespoke integration difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing triggers and enrolment rules cover much of the work. A small generator can combine approved modules without a language model.
tasks.still_hard: A welcome must feel relevant to different roles, languages and working patterns. Accessibility needs and late changes require exceptions; GDPR and national rules govern employee data and any consultation requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Create belonging, notice hesitation and turn abstract organisational objectives into a credible conversation.

ambition.what: Equivalent live orientation for off-cycle remote starters

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time scheduling and assembling packs, and more time with starters who need help connecting with the organisation. They can adjust cohort formats and content within the existing orientation remit; employment decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Design a short orientation learning sequence and evaluate understanding.
reach.learn: Learning objectives, accessible facilitation and measures beyond attendance.

evidence.claim: Starter-triggered scheduling, template assembly, enrolment and completion records can use deterministic software and existing configuration.
The supplied digest contains no orientation-specific product evidence or documented outcome; time estimates require local validation.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Shares cover the end-to-end process, including the hiring manager's contribution.
Role and location mappings select approved content; substantive content changes receive normal editorial approval.
Completion requires confirmed attendance or learning evidence, not merely a calendar invitation.
Existing connectors support starter events and bookings; otherwise integration effort increases.
Consultation effort depends on national rules and whether employee data use changes.
unknowns: Starter volumes, languages, locations and off-cycle coverage.
Existing enrolment, calendar and attendance interfaces.
Availability of approved, accessible orientation modules.
Who provides accurate attendance and team introduction confirmations.
Applicable access and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which scheduling exceptions account for most manual intervention?
Can starters in different working patterns receive an equivalent live welcome?
Which feedback measures show understanding and connection rather than attendance alone?
new_work: Maintain content modules and role-location mappings.
Handle unavailable speakers, late starters and accessibility requests.
Resolve missing attendance confirmations and failed enrolments.
Review feedback and refresh the orientation sequence.

tasks.short: Analyse compensation and benefits, then propose competitive and compliant policy changes.

steps.what: Export workforce, pay and benefit records for the review.
Reconcile population, pay definitions and employer costs.
Compare job scope and reward levels with relevant market benchmarks.

loop.input: Job descriptions, benchmark role definitions and an approved comparison rubric.
loop.output: Proposed benchmark matches with cited scope differences and explicit unmatched jobs.
loop.check: Validate benchmark identifiers; compensation specialist confirms scope, seniority and each accepted match.
loop.stop: One proposal and one correction pass per job; ambiguous jobs remain unmatched for specialist evaluation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Job titles and free-text responsibilities do not provide reliable exact matches.

steps.what: Model pay ranges, benefit options, distributional effects and budget trade-offs.
Check options against applicable law, collective agreements and benefit terms.
Draft proposed policy wording and explain the recommended option.

loop.input: Selected scenario, current policy and reviewed compliance advice.
loop.output: Policy redline and explanation tied to scenario identifiers.
loop.check: Compare every amount and eligibility condition with scenario fields; HR checks wording against legal advice.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved terms remain flagged for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy explanations and amendments vary with the selected trade-offs and existing wording.

steps.what: Discuss the proposal with employee representatives and record their response.
Approve the policy, budget and effective date after required consultation.
Publish the approved policy and retain its decision history.

tasks.design: Connect the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {ERP} to a governed baseline in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then calculate reward scenarios with deterministic rules and expose comparisons in the {BI}. Bounded loops propose benchmark matches and draft policy wording in the {DOCS}. Specialists validate matches and compliance, while consultation and leadership approval govern adoption.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pay definitions, job descriptions and purchased benchmarks rarely align cleanly. Scenario work becomes expensive when each review rebuilds mappings and reconciliations.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data mappings and calculation code cover the numerical work. Bounded models can compare job descriptions and draft explanations, with specialists checking their outputs.
tasks.still_hard: Market data licensing, comparable job scope and unexplained pay differences remain expensive. GDPR, the EU AI Act where applicable, collective agreements and national rules constrain data use, evaluation and policy adoption.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible trade-offs between competitiveness, fairness, affordability and employee expectations.
tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time reconciling files and rebuilding scenarios, and more time challenging job matches and reward trade-offs. They can recommend targeted budget changes more frequently; authority to set budgets or change individual pay still requires an explicit mandate.

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
reach.task: Evaluate benchmark matches and explain pay-range exceptions.
reach.learn: Job evaluation, survey comparability, benefit valuation and uncertainty in market samples.

reach.task: Translate approved reward policy into payroll parameter requirements.
reach.learn: Effective dating, taxable benefit treatment and reconciliation before implementation.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 supports recording job schemes for pay transparency; this supports structured records, not automated reward-policy decisions.
A UK university pilot graded 50 job descriptions with above 70% agreement with experts; this is limited, self-reported evidence.
The digest documents Dutch pay-transparency implementation proposals; other countries' implementation must be checked separately.
Specified employment evaluation uses fall within AI Act Annex III; applicability requires assessment of intended purpose.
Deterministic reconciliation and scenario calculations are feasible, but the digest supplies no measured outcome for this complete workflow.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Scope is one country, one reward framework and a limited benchmark dataset.
Benchmark licences permit the proposed processing and retained comparisons.
Comparisons inform policy proposals; individual pay changes require their own authorised process.
The organisation can configure controlled exports; unsupported interfaces increase integration effort.
Consultation ranges represent working effort. Statutory processes can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Applicable national pay-transparency, employment and representative consultation rules.
Benchmark licence terms, coverage and sample quality.
Consistency of job descriptions, grades, working hours and benefit valuations.
Available interfaces and authority to access identifiable pay data.
Who approves benchmark matches, budgets and policy changes.
Whether proposed job-matching functionality falls within regulated employment AI use.
research_questions: Can the baseline reproduce payroll and employer-cost control totals?
Which job matches remain unstable when titles are removed?
Can historical policy scenarios be reproduced without unexplained differences?
Which apparent pay gaps change materially after correcting hours, job scope and data errors?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation and benchmark matching exceptions.
Review proposed matches and policy redlines.
Maintain calculation rules, benchmark vintages and effective dates.
Monitor access, retention and benchmark licensing.
Refresh legal guidance and document consultation outcomes.
Review model changes against a fixed set of previously evaluated job descriptions.

role.altitude: The HR manager's week shifts toward negotiation, sensitive advice and evidence-based policy choices. Preparation and administration shrink, while authority over commitments, employment decisions and budgets remains subject to explicit mandates.
reach: Labor Relations Specialists: clause comparison and bargaining impact assessment.
Equal Opportunity Representatives and Officers: review patterns of unequal treatment.
Training and Development Specialists: orientation design and learning evaluation.
Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists: benchmark matching and reward analysis.
skills_to_grow: Define calculation assumptions and reconcile workforce data.
Review source-grounded drafts and recognise unsupported conclusions.
Design confidential case access and proportionate retention.
Evaluate job comparability and reward scenario uncertainty.
Translate national consultation requirements into workable approval steps.
Measure service quality alongside time saved.
role.ambitious_version: Run a regular people-policy review using validated reward scenarios, recurring advice themes and starter feedback, then bring concrete options to leaders and employee representatives. Preserve direct human access for sensitive cases and use explicit mandates for consequential decisions.
